examples.name: Default
examples.summary: Two bands stacked inside the column. The column draws the vertical rules; each band draws only its own horizontal ones, so no line is doubled.

examples.name: Widths
examples.summary: Three caps in one view — a width only reads against another.

examples.name: Bordered
examples.summary: With `bordered` off the column hands its sides to whatever frame encloses it.

examples.name: Padded
examples.summary: For a prose column with no modules, `padded` gives the column its own inset.

examples.name: WithModules
examples.summary: What the column is actually for: a stack of `Module` bands, with `Spacer` for the deliberate pauses between them. The column stays `:padded="false"` (the default) because each module already owns its inset; turning both on doubles the padding. The first module passes `:divided="false"` because its top edge is already drawn by the hero or the frame above it; every later one draws the seam above it, so a page never shows two hairlines on the same pixel. The last module sets `:padded="false"` so its grid runs to the column's rules and pads its own cells.
